title: P46 (Chester Beatty II): 2 Corinthians 6:3-7:4 (fols. 66v-67r)
source: P46 (Chester Beatty Biblical Papyrus II, Chester Beatty Library, Dublin): photographs as published in the INTF New Testament Virtual Manuscript Room; Greek from the INTF NTVMR transcription of P46; English from the King James Version
description: 2 Corinthians 6:3-7:4 in P46, the papyrus codex of Paul's letters copied around 200: fols. 66v-67r, each page with its photograph, the Greek transcription and the King James Version.
introduction:
P46 is a papyrus codex of the letters of Paul copied in Egypt around 200, the oldest surviving collection of Paul's letters. 86 of its 104 leaves survive: 56 in the Chester Beatty Library, Dublin (Biblical Papyrus II, published by Frederic Kenyon in 1934-1937) and 30 in the University of Michigan Library, Ann Arbor (P.Mich. inv. 6238, published by Henry Sanders in 1935). The letters run in the order Romans, Hebrews, 1 and 2 Corinthians, Ephesians, Galatians, Philippians, Colossians and 1 Thessalonians; the first seven leaves (Romans 1:1-5:17) and the end of the book are lost. Hebrews standing after Romans, and the doxology of Romans (16:25-27) standing after 15:33, are among its best-known features.

Each section below is one page side: the holding library's photograph, the NTVMR diplomatic transcription line by line, and the King James Version of every verse that has text on the page. The lower lines of many leaves are lost; the transcribers' restorations are in square brackets.

This entry covers fols. 66v-67r (2 Corinthians 6:3-7:4).
translator_notes: Greek: the NTVMR diplomatic transcription, line by line as on the papyrus. Square brackets enclose letters that are lost or illegible and were supplied by the transcribers; a dot under a letter marks it as uncertain; [...] marks a gap. Nomina sacra and numerals keep the scribe's overline. Spelling is the scribe's (no accents or breathings). Words broken at a line end stay broken as on the papyrus. Corrections are not shown: the text is the first hand.

English: the King James Version (1611), whole verses, for every verse that has text on the page. A verse that begins on one page and ends on the next is given in full on both. The KJV translates a later form of the Greek text, so its wording does not always match the papyrus; material differences (such as verses the papyrus does not have) are noted in the section.

translation.text: <sup>6:3</sup>Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed: <sup>4</sup>But in all things approving ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses, <sup>5</sup>In stripes, in imprisonments, in tumults, in labours, in watchings, in fastings; <sup>6</sup>By pureness, by knowledge, by longsuffering, by kindness, by the Holy Ghost, by love unfeigned, <sup>7</sup>By the word of truth, by the power of God, by the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left, <sup>8</sup>By honour and dishonour, by evil report and good report: as deceivers, and yet true; <sup>9</sup>As unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and, behold, we live; as chastened, and not killed; <sup>10</sup>As sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things. <sup>11</sup>O ye Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you, our heart is enlarged. <sup>12</sup>Ye are not straitened in us, but ye are straitened in your own bowels. <sup>13</sup>Now for a recompence in the same, (I speak as unto my children,) be ye also enlarged.

translation.text: <sup>6:14</sup>Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness? <sup>15</sup>And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel? <sup>16</sup>And what agreement hath the temple of God with idols? for ye are the temple of the living God; as God hath said, I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. <sup>17</sup>Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you, <sup>18</sup>And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty. <sup>7:1</sup>Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God. <sup>2</sup>Receive us; we have wronged no man, we have corrupted no man, we have defrauded no man. <sup>3</sup>I speak not this to condemn you: for I have said before, that ye are in our hearts to die and live with you. <sup>4</sup>Great is my boldness of speech toward you, great is my glorying of you: I am filled with comfort, I am exceeding joyful in all our tribulation.
